title: Standings double-counts and splits teams, producing an incorrect Brasileirao table
evidence: soccer_data.erl:7,11 loads BOTH Brasileirao_Matches.csv (label "Brasileirao") and novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv (label "Brasileirao Historical"); seasons 2012-2019 overlap and contain the SAME physical matches (verified: 27/04/2019 Flamengo 3-1 Cruzeiro appears in both; each file has exactly 380 rows for 2019). The default standings competition "Brasileirao" (soccer_mcp.erl:13) is matched by a case-insensitive SUBSTRING filter (soccer_query.erl:15 contains/2), so it matches BOTH labels and feeds 760 matches into the 2019 table. Separately soccer_query.erl:45 add_table/add_side keys the table by the RAW team name (maps:get(home,M)/maps:get(away,M)), and the two files spell the same club differently ("Flamengo-RJ" vs "Flamengo", "Palmeiras-SP" vs "Palmeiras"), so each team splits into two rows each holding half the season. _factual.json score 0.0: no tool returned a usable 2019 Serie A table. standings_test (soccer_tests.erl:8) passes but actually encodes the split (sample has "Palmeiras-SP" and "Palmeiras" as separate rows).
suggestion: Key the standings table by normalized team name (home_normalized/away_normalized), and either dedupe overlapping matches across the two Brasileirao files or make the competition filter an exact-label match instead of a substring match.
